reviews.title: Looks great fundamentally different from older monitor styles
reviews.comment: Looks amazing. One thing that confused me at first was my dual monitor windows getting rearranged every time I powered it off. I was used to plugging both my monitors into a power strip and turning that off when I put my PC to sleep. This monitor likes to retain power so it can perform a "Pixel refresh" and will give you a warning that it didn't get to do it if you remove its power which is kinda annoying. So I just plugged it into my other power strip that I never turn off and problem solved. It goes into a low power mode anyway so it's probably fine.
reviews.author: Ryan C.

reviews.title: A worthwhile upgrade for my setup!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1bJJd8BSxL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71P6kxsP5GL._SY256.jpg Upgrading this from an LG Ultragear 1440p 144hz monitor, which was also 27 inches in size.
This is my first ever OLED display of any kind and I've heard so many great things about them, mainly how the colors and blacks are super vibrant.
I have decided to stick with 2560x1440, since that's the resolution I like to play all of my games on and the upgraded refresh rate from 144hz to 240hz is super helpful for fast paced and action packed competitive PvP titles such as Fortnite, CS2, Overwatch, etc etc.
Even games that aren't necessarily PvP look amazing on this monitor, great examples I've shown such as Helldivers 2, Genshin Impact. Honkai Star Rail, Zenless Zone Zero, BeamNG Drive and Red Dead Redemption are fantastic to look at thanks to the OLED display's eye popping colors.
It's also great to know that this monitor can do certain things my old one could not, such as being able to adjust the height of the stand and to rotate it horizontally. The latter I have no reason to do so but if you're looking for a monitor for horizontal use and would like the advantages of an OLED display, look no further than this.
At the time of purchase of this display, it supposedly comes with a free Steam key for the newly released Resident Evil: Requiem. I have yet to receive it but when I do, I'll update this review to show off how the game looks on this display.
I'm using this with my PC equipped with a Ryzen 7 9700X and a GeForce RTX 5060 Ti with 16GB of video memory using a DisplayPort cable and it's running all of my favorite games at 1440p at 240hz refresh rate.
This display also does support both NVIDIA's G-Sync for GTX/RTX GPUs (despite the product details here NOT mentioning it) and AMD's FreeSync for Radeon GPUs, which does help smooth things out on the display as much as possible.
Maybe next time I'll go for a 4K OLED monitor with a high refresh rate when, and if (a big IF) those drop in price.

reviews.title: Excellent Gaming Monitor - some caveats
reviews.comment:
While the monitor did not initially work with the full refresh rate at first, this was due to my Mac and not the monitor itself. Once I got the right cable, I was able to go all the way up to 240Hz with VRR. I was also able to enable HDR with the new cable. I viewed a couple of “OLED Test” videos, and they looked stunning with the OLED blacks and vibrant colors. Games also look great. (Pics don’t do it justice)
This monitor does suffer from a couple of shortcomings that are inherent to OLED displays. First, the pixel shifting IS noticeable. As you’re watching the screen, the screen will slightly “shift” to help keep the pixels from burning in. Second, there is noticeable text fringing. Due to the separate RGB lights for each pixel, there can be a slight colored border found mostly around white text.
If you can overlook the above flaws, mostly just inherent to OLED displays, it's a great display for multimedia.
